subject.title: refactor: separate external conversations from local sessions

question: Should OpenClaw adopt these conversation tools, Gateway methods, and v11 durable-delivery schema as the permanent core boundary between external transport addresses and local sessions?
rationale: This PR creates new public tool/protocol surfaces and persisted semantics across core, plugins, clients, and upgrades; repository policy cannot choose that lasting product contract without owner intent.

options.title: Approve with proof gates
options.body: Accept the proposed core boundary, but require live Reef round-trip/recovery evidence and fresh-plus-upgrade validation before merge.

options.title: Narrow the rollout
options.body: Split the generic conversation registry/API and migration from Reef-specific delivery and native-client exposure so each contract can be reviewed independently.

options.title: Pause the core feature
options.body: Keep using explicit message targets and local session tools until the long-term conversation API and persistence model are redesigned or sponsored.

recommendation.title: Approve with proof gates
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed core boundary, but require live Reef round-trip/recovery evidence and fresh-plus-upgrade validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the linked product proposal, assignment, and complete implementation sequence, making them the best available person to confirm or route the intended contract.
